**Three Lane B direction briefs (proposals only)**

P1, 'Daylight drafting, faithful refinement':
- **Changes:** finish DESIGN.md conformance on every surface, legacy and internal included; resolve the DESIGN.md contradictions; ship real or self-hosted fonts; unify the two anonymous landings into one hero, scatter and thin footer with legal links; adopt the plain-word status vocabulary; set dark mode aside until it is deliberately designed.

- **Risks:** little visible novelty; a large diff across legacy surfaces; licensed fonts are a protected purchase, and the free analogs 'should not ship'.

P2, 'Engineering-console accents, diagram-inspired and scoped':
- **Changes:** keep bone daylight for every customer quoting surface. Add a scoped console token set (charcoal canvas, small mono labels, thin outlined boxes, right-angle connectors, restrained mint/cyan, lavender and pale-blue role colors, top-down flow with checkpoints) used only on JARVIS/engineering surfaces and process diagrams such as the status timeline, request-progress views and docs diagrams.

- **Keeps:** the customer palette, layout, typography roles and the single accent on quote decisions.
- **Risks:** directly contradicts DESIGN.md's single accent, no multi-color systems, purple/violet and blue bans, and 'defense-tech black' rejection, so it needs a Decisions row. Two visual languages could fragment the brand. Mint/cyan on charcoal must be contrast-checked. The liked reference covers diagrams, not app chrome.

P3, 'Drawing-sheet title block, monochrome print':
- **Changes:** restructure page chrome into engineering-drawing sheets: zone grid references on the frame, a bottom-right title block holding part number, revision and status, no surface tints at all (ink, bone and hairline only), no cards anywhere, tables for every collection, and the accent only on the single current decision. - **Keeps:** bone, ink, the oxidized red, mono data and the scatter-first comparison.
- **Risks:** the frame chrome costs vertical space on phones; risk of ornament against DESIGN.md's 'Decoration level: minimal'; could feel cold to students and tinkerers; a larger layout refactor than P1.
